canonical_name: Sylow existence, conjugacy, and counting theorem family for finite groups
literal_source_claim_zh: 有限群中p-子群的存在性、共轭性和计数
literal_source_claim_en: Existence, conjugacy, and counting of p-subgroups in finite groups.
source_attribution: Ludwig Sylow, 1872 (catalog metadata corroborated by the inspected historical paper)
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For every finite group G and prime p, a Sylow p-subgroup of maximal p-power order exists; every two Sylow p-subgroups are conjugate; and their number is congruent to one modulo p and satisfies the selected Sylow-index and normalizer-index counting clauses.
statement_blocker: The catalog names the existence, conjugacy, and counting family but gives no definition, binders, formulas, or counting clauses. An accepted source crosswalk must select maximality versus maximal-prime-power order, Finite versus Fintype, explicit conjugacy encoding, all required count clauses, the historical substitution-group to arbitrary finite-group bridge, and boundary cases before one exact conjunction can be elaborated.
domain_and_universes: Candidate scope: G : Type u with Group G and Finite G; p : Nat with p.Prime; Sylow p G as maximal p-subgroups. Exact universes, finite-carrier encoding, implicit instances, Nat.card coercions, normalizer carrier, and source-approved maximal-order equivalence remain statement-phase decisions.
conclusion: Open as one exact expression: the target must jointly cover source-approved existence, conjugacy, and counting clauses without dropping or broadening any branch.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake. The statement must explicitly settle p not dividing the group order, the trivial group, p = 2, p-groups, normal Sylow subgroups, and finite-typeclass representation.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Nonempty (Sylow p G) together with a maximal-order characterization
existence of a subgroup whose cardinality is p raised to the p-adic multiplicity of Nat.card G
transitivity of the conjugation action, or an explicit element conjugating every pair of Sylow p-subgroups
Nat.card (Sylow p G) congruent to one modulo p
the Sylow count divides the index of a Sylow subgroup and equals the index of its normalizer
a conjunction or package assembling all source-approved clauses
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: p does not divide Nat.card G, so the trivial subgroup is the unique Sylow p-subgroup
the trivial finite group and singleton carrier
a Sylow p-subgroup is normal and consequently unique
Finite G versus Fintype G and induced finiteness of Sylow p G
maximal p-subgroup versus exact maximal-prime-power cardinality
Subgroup.normalizer applied to a subgroup or its underlying set
excluded_substitutions: only one of existence, conjugacy, or counting substituted for the three-part catalog family
existence of an arbitrary p-subgroup without maximality or maximal-prime-power order
only the congruence count when the approved target also includes divisibility or normalizer index
Cauchy's theorem, Lagrange's theorem, Hall subgroup theory, or a generic group-action result without checked assembly
a structure, hypothesis, or typeclass that assumes the desired Sylow conclusions as data
the untrusted catalog label verified, a declaration name, a #check, or an upstream URL as proof credit
